Job Details: 
 Job Description: 
 At Intel, we are building the next generation of software technologies that unlock the potential of heterogeneous computing. Our compiler technologies help developers harness CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators through high-performance, portable software.
 As an intern, you will contribute to an open ecosystem that advances performance, scalability, reliability, and developer productivity for AI, HPC, and other demanding workloads, while supporting Intel's commitment to contributing to and collaborating with open-source communities.
 About the Team 
 The Intel Compiler Engineering Team develops LLVM-based C, C++, SYCL, Triton, MLIR, Domain Specific Languages (DSLs), and Fortran compiler technologies for Intel processor platforms, including CPUs and GPUs.
 The team works across the compiler stack and in close collaboration with hardware architecture teams, covering language front ends, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, debug information, runtimes, offload support, quality, and developer tooling. This work connects Intel hardware and compiler capabilities with AI frameworks and software ecosystems such as PyTorch, inference engines, and machine-learning models.
 You will collaborate with experienced engineers and contribute to open-source communities while learning how production compilers are designed, tested, optimized, and delivered.
 Position Overview 
 We are hiring a Compiler Engineer Intern to contribute to Intel's compiler software stack. You will work with experienced compiler and hardware architecture engineers on a scoped project that may involve:
 Compiler features or MLIR-based intermediate representations 
 Triton or other Domain Specific Languages (DSLs) 
 Optimization, code generation, runtime, or offload support 
 Debug information or testing infrastructure 
 Performance analysis or developer tools 
 Projects may involve connecting software capabilities to AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning models such as DeepSeek, Hugging Face, and Kimi.
 You will investigate technical problems, implement and test solutions, analyze results, and communicate findings to the team. This opportunity is designed for an undergraduate student who wants to build practical compiler-engineering experience and apply foundational computer science concepts to production software.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Contribute to the design, implementation, testing, or analysis of compiler and runtime technologies 
 Develop and debug software in C or C++ within a large, collaborative codebase 
 Create or improve tests, reproduce defects, analyze failures, and help deliver reliable solutions 
 Evaluate functional correctness, compile-time behavior, runtime performance, or code quality, as applicable to the project 
 Participate in code reviews, technical discussions, and project planning with mentors and team members 
 Document designs, experiments, results, and lessons learned, and present project outcomes to the team 
 Contribute to open-source projects when aligned with the assigned work 
 To Be Successful in This Role 
 You should demonstrate the following professional traits:
 Curiosity and willingness to learn unfamiliar technologies 
 Strong analytical, problem-solving, and debugging skills 
 Clear written and verbal communication 
 Qualifications: 
 This position is not eligible for intel immigration sponsorship. 
 Minimum Qualifications 
 Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Informatics, or a related technical discipline 
 3+ months of coursework or project experience in data structures, algorithms, computer architecture, operating systems, programming languages, or compiler construction 
 Experience programming in C++ through coursework, research, personal projects, or prior internships 
 Experience using software development and debugging tools in a Linux or similar development environment 
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Compiler-related coursework or project experience, including parsing, intermediate representations, optimization, code generation, or runtimes 
 Hands-on compiler development experience with LLVM, MLIR, Triton, GCC, Clang, or similar compiler frameworks 
 Experience with GPU programming models such as CUDA, SYCL, OpenMP, or HIP 
 Knowledge of CPU or GPU architecture, heterogeneous computing, or systems programming 
 Familiarity with AI frameworks such as PyTorch, inference engines such as vLLM and SGLang, and machine-learning model ecosystems such as DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi 
 Tile-based programming model knowledge 
 GPU compute kernel writing experience 
 Experience with Git, automated testing, continuous integration, performance analysis, or open-source development 
 Technical contributions such as code, patches, reviews, research, publications, or substantial academic projects

Student / Intern

Shift 1 (Canada)

Canada, Toronto

About the role and team 
In this role, you will be the engine behind Uber Eats' growth, responsible for bringing the best local and regional small and medium merchants onto our platform. This isn't a typical sales job-it's about navigating the messy reality of cold-calling, handling frequent rejection, and winning over busy business owners who don't always have a script.
Success here requires a mix of grit and resourcefulness. You'll need to thrive in a high-volume, high-stakes environment where you're expected to make 50+ dials a day while maintaining the energy to close deals in person. If you are resilient, energized by ambitious quotas, and ready to take total ownership of your territory, this is where you'll grow.
 What you'll do 
 Own and manage a high-volume pipeline of local merchants, using a mix of persistent cold-calling and in-person meetings to sign new partnerships.
 Navigate tough contract negotiations to establish sustainable economics for both the partner and Uber, ensuring a strong foundation for long-term collaboration.
 Communicate the value of Uber's products with clarity and conviction, acting as an ambassador to develop trust with skeptical prospects.
 Collaborate cross-functionally with Operations and Account Management teams to unblock dependencies and ensure a seamless onboarding experience for new partners.
 Adapt your approach based on shifting market dynamics and daily performance metrics to consistently exceed monthly sales targets.
 Basic Qualifications 
 Minimum 1+ years total professional sales experience or 0+ years with a Bachelor's Degree (earned or in progress) and exposure to sales through internships or other experiences
 Preferred Qualifications 
 Experience managing a full sales cycle and using CRM tools like Salesforce.
 Resilience and a \"roll up your sleeves\" mindset with a high tolerance for cold-calling and rejection.
 Strong curiosity and critical thinking skills to solve merchant problems on your feet.
 Background in e-commerce, restaurant, or hospitality commercial environments.
For Canada-based roles: The base hourly rate for this role is CAD $25.73 per hour - CAD $27.17 per hour. Additionally, our Sales Representatives are eligible to participate in the Company's Incentive program and will be eligible for a cash variable incentive target of CAD $35,679 - CAD $37,676 annually based on individual sales performance, with any amount of incentive payment based on the terms of the Sales Incentive Plan.
You may be offered an equity award & other types of comp. You will also be eligible for various benefits.
 Ready to Ride? 
This isn't the kind of place where you follow a playbook - it's where you help write one. If you're driven by impact, energized by challenge, and ready to shape how the world moves - we'd love to hear from you.
You may be eligible for bonuses, equity, and other compensation, as well as a range of benefits. Explore our benefits. 
Offices remain key to collaboration and Uber's culture. Unless approved for full remote work, employees must spend at least 50% of their time in-office. Some roles, like those at greenlight hubs, require full-time in-office presence. Ask your Recruiter for details about this role's requirements.

 L'objectif de l'architecte de l'information est de définir la structure globale, les normes et l'intégration des systèmes de données afin de garantir que les données sont organisées, accessibles et alignées sur les besoins de l'entreprise.

The Company 
 Versaterm is a PE-backed, high-growth SaaS company building a fully integrated platform across the entire public safety ecosystem — dispatch, law enforcement, forensics, courts, and beyond . We've grown through strategic acquisitions and deep product investment. What connects all of it is a single purpose: give public safety agencies the tools and insights to make better decisions in high-stakes moments. 
 When a 911 call is answered, a detective investigates a case, or a forensic lab processes evidence, there's a good chance our software is working behind the scenes. That's been true for over four decades. 
 AI is central to where we're going. Not as a feature but as core infrastructure. We're embedding intelligence directly into the workflows our customers rely on every day, and we're doing it alongside them. Our customers tell us what the mission demands. We build what answers it. 
 This work attracts a specific kind of person — someone who wants to be pushed by great people, build things that outlast a sprint cycle, and go home knowing the work connected back to something real. 
 The Role 
 The Director of Customer Success leads the post-sale customer lifecycle across all customer segments, ensuring customers realize measurable value, adopt solutions effectively, and renew and expand over time. This role is accountable for building and scaling a high-performing Customer Success organization operating under a “One Account, One Owner” model, with clear ownership of customer outcomes across Strategic, Enterprise, State, and Transactional accounts. 
 The Director defines how Customer Success operates—establishing engagement models, operating cadence, and cross-functional alignment—while ensuring consistent execution across the core pillars of Strategic Engagement, Adoption, Expansion, and Retention. Joignez-vous à l’équipe d’EDC! 
 À Exportation et développement Canada (EDC), nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger.  Poste : Gestionnaire, Recherches sectorielles

 Détail de la rémunération 
 Facilitation des ventes (stratégie et gouvernement) 19 : Les salaires annuels varient généralement de 112 006 $ à 149 341 $, plus une rémunération au rendement, en fonction des qualifications et de l’expérience. 
 Lieu de travail 
 Exportation et développement Canada évolue dans un environnement de travail hybride, avec une exigence actuelle de présence au bureau trois jours par semaine.
 Ce rôle sera exercé à partir du siège social d’EDC à Ottawa.

 Employés internes : veuillez consulter l’article de ServiceNow intitulé « Mouvements internes – Ce qu’il faut savoir ». 
 À propos d’EDC 
 À Exportation et développement Canada (EDC), nous aidons les entreprises canadiennes à réussir à l’étranger. Société d’État à vocation financière, EDC propose des solutions financières innovantes et des conseils d’experts pour aider les entreprises à explorer de nouveaux marchés, à atténuer leurs risques et à se développer. 
 Pourquoi vous joindre à EDC? 
 Gamme complète d’avantages sociaux : EDC offre un régime de rémunération et d’avantages sociaux concurrentiel, une bonne conciliation travail-vie personnelle et la chance de contribuer à bâtir un Canada et un monde meilleurs grâce au commerce. 
 Conciliation travail-vie personnelle : EDC offre un régime de rémunération concurrentiel et un équilibre travail-vie personnelle. Nous proposons des modalités de travail hybride, de trois à quatre semaines de vacances payées, une période de fermeture collective, des vendredis raccourcis en été. 
 Perfectionnement professionnel : Profitez de nos occasions d’apprentissage continu, notamment des programmes de formation, des ateliers et de la formation linguistique. 
 Culture inclusive : Intégrez un milieu de travail diversifié et inclusif qui fait une place de choix à l’équité en matière d’emploi et valorise la diversité des idées, des forces et des origines pour favoriser la réussite. 
 Programmes de bien-être : Nous offrons des initiatives de bien-être, de l’aide à la santé mentale et des programmes de conditionnement physique pour veiller à votre santé et à votre bonheur. 
 Investissement dans la collectivité :  Participez à des activités de bénévolat et donnez au suivant grâce à un éventail de programmes de responsabilité sociale. 
 Aperçu de l’équipe 
 L’Équipe des secteurs et services consultatifs internationaux aide les entreprises canadiennes à se développer à l’international en combinant une expertise sectorielle, des renseignements concrets sur les marchés, des conseils stratégiques et un réseau pouvant déboucher sur des occasions d’affaires à l’échelle mondiale. L’équipe élabore et met en œuvre les stratégies sectorielles prioritaires d’EDC et collabore avec l’ensemble de l’organisation afin de transformer les connaissances relatives aux capacités canadiennes, aux chaînes de valeur mondiales et aux besoins du marché en choix concrets et en occasions pour les exportateurs. 
 À titre de gestionnaire, Recherches sectorielles, la personne choisie dirigera et perfectionnera une équipe chargée de mener des recherches sur les écosystèmes d’affaires canadiens, les secteurs et sous-secteurs industriels, ainsi que les chaînes de valeur mondiales. 
 La personne choisie jouera à la fois le rôle de coéquipier et d’accompagnateur : elle établira les priorités, créera les conditions propices à un rendement d’équipe optimal et continuera de participer activement à des travaux de recherche et d’analyse de grande valeur, ainsi qu’à l’élaboration de conclusions et de recommandations destinées à la direction. 
 Elle fera preuve de discernement, de curiosité et d’un esprit ouvert à l’expérimentation pour aborder des questions de recherche complexes. Elle veillera à ce que les chercheurs déterminent les parties prenantes pertinentes pour chaque mandat et sachent déterminer quand il peut être opportun de collaborer ou de confier le dossier à une autre équipe afin d’approfondir la recherche ou d’obtenir un soutien spécialisé. Son travail aidera EDC à déterminer les domaines dans lesquels les capacités canadiennes répondent à la demande internationale et les secteurs dans lesquels EDC peut générer les plus grandes retombées possibles. Cette personne relèvera de la vice-présidente ou du vice-président, Secteurs et Services consultatifs internationaux.

 Diriger, encadrer et perfectionner une équipe de chercheurs en définissant des objectifs clairs, en répartissant les tâches de manière réfléchie, en fournissant des commentaires en temps opportun, en favorisant la croissance professionnelle et en créant un environnement d’équipe axé sur l’inclusion, la collaboration et la responsabilité. 
 Définir et gérer le programme et le portefeuille de recherche de l’équipe, en trouvant un équilibre entre les priorités stratégiques, les nouveaux besoins opérationnels, les capacités, les échéanciers et la nécessité d’assurer à la fois des résultats rapides et un travail d’analyse approfondi. 
 Continuer d’être un chercheur de terrain en dirigeant des études ciblées et hautement prioritaires portant sur les entreprises, les écosystèmes sectoriels et sous-sectoriels canadiens, les dynamiques concurrentielles, les technologies ainsi que les chaînes de valeur nationales et mondiales. 
 Analyser des enjeux commerciaux et sectoriels complexes, choisir des méthodes qualitatives et quantitatives adaptées à l’objectif fixé, et intégrer la recherche primaire, les sources secondaires, les données au niveau des entreprises et les renseignements financiers et sur le marché. 
 Établir et respecter des normes en matière de qualité de la recherche, d’intégrité des sources, de rigueur analytique, d’utilisation responsable des outils axés sur l’IA, d’évaluation par les pairs, de documentation et de communication claire des hypothèses et des limites. 
 Traduire des données complexes en stratégies sectorielles concrètes, en évaluations d’occasions d’affaires, en profils d’entreprises et d’écosystèmes, en notes d’information, en présentations et en recommandations qui facilitent l’établissement des priorités et la prise de décisions. 
 Relier les capacités canadiennes à la demande internationale en aidant à cerner les lacunes, les occasions liées à la chaîne d’approvisionnement et les domaines où les renseignements, les services consultatifs, les capacités de développement des marchés, le réseau et les solutions financières d’EDC peuvent favoriser la croissance des exportateurs. 
 Établir des relations de confiance au sein d’EDC ainsi qu’avec des experts externes, des associations sectorielles, des partenaires gouvernementaux, des entreprises et des organismes de recherche afin de vérifier des hypothèses, d’élargir la base de données probantes et d’accroître la portée et l’utilité des renseignements. 
 Créer des outils réutilisables, des ensembles de données, des référentiels et des pratiques de partage des connaissances qui améliorent la productivité de l’équipe, renforcent les connaissances institutionnelles et rendent les renseignements accessibles à des publics non experts. 
 Surveiller la mise en œuvre, les répercussions des recherches, les besoins des parties prenantes et les nouvelles tendances; ajuster les priorités à mesure que les données probantes évoluent et communiquer les progrès, les risques et les recommandations à la haute direction. 
 Ce que nous cherchons: 
 Diplôme universitaire en économie, en sciences politiques, en administration des affaires, en affaires internationales, en sciences des données ou en sciences sociales, ou dans un domaine connexe; une combinaison équivalente d’étude et d’expérience peut être considérée

 Expérience avérée en gestion du personnel, notamment en ce qui concerne la définition des attentes, l’accompagnement et le perfectionnement des employés, la formulation de commentaires constructifs, la gestion du rendement, la promotion du bien-être et la constitution d’une équipe inclusive et hautement performante 
 Solide expérience en tant que chercheur de terrain, capable de structurer et de mener à bien de manière autonome des projets complexes, tout en supervisant un portefeuille plus vaste et en permettant à ses collègues d’atteindre leurs objectifs

 Expérience en matière de recherche primaire et secondaire, d’analyse de profils d’entreprises, d’ensembles de données au niveau de la Société, d’évaluation de la taille des marchés, d’analyse concurrentielle, ainsi que des plateformes pertinentes de renseignements commerciaux, sur les marchés et les secteurs

WHO ARE WE?

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


 

Role overview:

North is Cohere’s AI workspace platform for enterprises: a secure, customizable environment where companies can use AI across their real workflows while maintaining control over sensitive data. North connects AI agents with workplace tools, applications, and business context, helping users delegate complex work, build automations, inspect outputs, and collaborate with AI in production environments.



As North becomes more capable, one of the most important questions is also one of the hardest: how do we know whether the model is actually getting better for the workflows customers care about?



This role is about being the voice of North inside modelling. You will build the evaluation systems, feedback loops, and applied modelling workflows that make sure model progress translates into better product outcomes for North users. You will work closely with North product teams, customer-facing teams, and modelling teams to define what “good” means across the product surface, turn real usage and product direction into high-quality evals, and use those evals to guide model selection, patches, and regular model updates.



This is neither a pure research role nor a conventional product engineering role. It is a rigorous applied MLE role for someone who cares deeply about measurement, model behavior, and real-world product quality. You should be excited by the craft of building careful evals: evals that capture messy agentic workflows, reflect actual customer needs, resist superficial benchmark hacking, and provide useful signal for where the product and models need to go next.

 Client & Project Leadership

 Curate and maintain organized, prioritized backlogs that keep project teams focused and work moving forward.

 Personally handle "quick win" Drupal and/or WordPress site configurations, content entry, and initial bug troubleshooting before escalating to the development team. 
 Collaborate with clients and internal teams to resolve blockers and anticipate needs.
 Forecast and coordinate internal resources, including front-end and back-end developers, UX/UI designers, and strategists, based on timing, scope, and expertise.
 Quality, Budget, and Timeline Oversight
 Review completed work (designs, tickets, content, and development) to ensure it meets Kanopi's quality standards before client handoff.
 Monitor and forecast budgets and timelines to ensure tasks are completed on time and within scope, while providing regular updates to clients and Kanopi management on hours used and project progress.
 Flag risks early and lead the team in resolving and mitigating issues.
 Expedite urgent requests, triage issues quickly, and manage escalations, particularly within support accounts.

 Monitor team workloads and pacing to help maintain a sustainable, healthy balance, identifying early signs of strain or burnout in yourself and others and proactively adjusting priorities when needed.

 Mentor and support other project managers, sharing best practices and serving as a go-to resource for the PM team.

 Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.

 Have a proven track record managing the full life cycle of web build projects, as well as long-term client support engagements.

 Créer et gérer la feuille de route numérique continue sur trois ans; ce document établit l’ordre d’obtention des résultats requis à l’atteinte de l’état cible technologique et facilite celle-ci dans tous les secteurs de l’organisation. 
 Demeurer aux faits des tendances sectorielles et des technologies émergentes pour qu’EDC dispose des outils numériques qui assureront sa pertinence sur le marché afin d’accroître la présence commerciale du Canada sur la scène internationale. 
 Voir à la mise en œuvre intégrée des projets sur le plan du numérique, des données, des infrastructures et de la cybersécurité pour offrir une excellente expérience aux clients, aux utilisateurs et aux employés. 
 L’Équipe des technologies, Crimes financiers – Connaître son client (CF – CSC) d’EDC est à la recherche d’une analyste principale ou d’un analyste principal des systèmes de gestion. 
 L’Équipe met en place et améliore des capacités technologiques indispensables à la mission d’EDC en ce qu’elles lui permettent de gérer les risques liés au crime financier, à la clientèle, aux contreparties, aux règlements et aux activités. Elle soutient, par exemple, les processus de connaissance du client, de contrôle préalable des clients et des contreparties, de filtrage, d’évaluation du risque, de gestion des dossiers et de conformité. 
 La personne choisie fera le lien entre des experts internes et les équipes de prestation de solutions technologiques. Elle traduira les besoins d’ordre commercial, réglementaire, informationnel et pratique en exigences claires et en livrables de déploiement adéquats. 
 La personne choisie travaillera dans un environnement matriciel avec des spécialistes du crime financier et de la connaissance du client, des équipes de produits et de plateformes et des fournisseurs en architecture, en données, en cybersécurité et en technologie. Elle aidera ces groupes à convenir d’une même compréhension des problèmes commerciaux, des résultats attendus des solutions, des exigences, des contraintes, des contrôles et des priorités d’implantation. 
 Il s’agit d’un poste de collaborateur individuel principal. Vous aurez à diriger des analyses complexes, à faciliter les décisions, à remettre en question les hypothèses de manière constructive, à déceler les répercussions interfonctionnelles et à contribuer à l’élaboration continue des analyses concernant les systèmes de gestion et les pratiques de déploiement de l’équipe. 
 Ce que vous ferez : 
 Diriger les étapes de découverte et d’analyse pour des initiatives complexes en clarifiant les problèmes à résoudre, les résultats voulus, la portée, les hypothèses, les contraintes, les liens de dépendance et les risques. 
 Découvrir, analyser, valider, prioriser et gérer les exigences commerciales, fonctionnelles, non fonctionnelles et relatives aux données, aux intégrations et aux contrôles. 
 Traduire les obligations réglementaires, les politiques, les décisions relatives aux risques et les besoins pratiques en règles de fonctionnement, en processus, en exigences, en critères d’acceptation et en résultats vérifiables. 
 Consigner les processus actuels et futurs, les parcours utilisateur, la logique décisionnelle, les besoins de données, les interactions des systèmes de même que les répercussions sur les applications et les équipes touchées. 
 Produire des documents utiles, comme des récits d’utilisation, des modèles procéduraux, des règles de fonctionnement, des cartes de données, des exigences d’interface, des registres de traçabilité et des scénarios d’essai. 
 Animer des ateliers et faciliter la prise de décisions pour les équipes chargées des affaires, de la conformité, des risques, des données, de l’architecture, de la sécurité, du déploiement et des fournisseurs. 
 Repérer les lacunes et les conflits éventuels, évaluer les options et les compromis et mener les parties prenantes à des décisions claires et documentées. 
 Collaborer avec les responsables de produits et les équipes de déploiement pour affiner le cahier des charges, établir les priorités et garder le cap sur la feuille de route de la plateforme relative aux crimes financiers et à la connaissance du client. 
 Soutenir la conception de solutions, les tests, les essais d’acceptation par l’utilisateur, les implantations, la préparation pratique et les validations subséquentes. 
 Fournir des vérifications par les pairs, des guides pratiques et des méthodes réutilisables qui améliorent la qualité des analyses des systèmes de gestion et l’uniformité de l’équipe. 
 Ce que nous cherchons: 
 Diplôme en affaires, en technologie, en génie, en systèmes informatiques ou dans un domaine connexe, ou combinaison équivalente d’études et d’expérience pertinentes.
 Au moins sept années d’expérience pertinente et progressive en analyse de systèmes de gestion pour des transformations complexes reposant sur la technologie, en tant qu’analyste d’affaires, analyste des systèmes de gestion ou autre poste comparable.
 Expérience au sein d’un environnement très réglementé, comme les services financiers, la conformité relative au crime financier, la connaissance du client, l’intégration de clients ou de contreparties ou le filtrage.
 Capacité avérée à traduire des besoins relatifs aux affaires, aux règlements, aux risques, aux données, à la sécurité et aux contrôles en exigences claires et éprouvables et en artéfacts de déploiement.
 Expérience couvrant l’ensemble de cycle de vie de solutions allant de la découverte et de la conception jusqu’aux essais, à la mise en œuvre et à la préparation pratique, en suivant un modèle de déploiement Agile, hybride ou comparable.
 Excellentes compétences en analyse, en présentation, en communication écrite et en gestion des parties prenantes, ce qui comprend la clarification d’exigences qui semblent contradictoires et d’ambiguïtés.
 Expérience d’utilisation d’Azure DevOps, ou d’un cahier de charges comparable, et d’un outil de gestion des exigences.
 Ce qui vous distinguera : 
 Expérience directe en connaissance du client, en contrôle préalable, en filtrage relatif aux sanctions ou aux listes de surveillance, en évaluation du risque associé aux clients ou aux contreparties, en gestion de dossiers ou en surveillance continue. 
 Expérience en mise en œuvre de technologies configurables liées au crime financier, aux processus, à des intégrations ou à la gestion de dossiers, par exemple le module de service à la clientèle ServiceNow et des outils de filtrage tels que Ripjar, Actimize ou FinScan. 
 Expérience en cartographie de données, en règles de qualité des données, en interfaces système, en interfaces de programmation d’application, en intégrations par lots ou en implantation de produits externes. 
 Certification reconnue en analyse des systèmes de gestion, par exemple : attestation Certified Business Analysis Professional (CBAP) de l’IIBA, Agile Analysis Certification (AAC) de l’IIBA ou Professional in Business Analysis du PMI. 
 Maîtrise des deux langues officielles.

About Valsoft 
 Valsoft builds and scales vertical market software companies. We partner with strong teams, invest in the long term, and run disciplined operating systems to drive sustainable growth across our portfolio.
 About BluSynq 
 BluSynq is changing the way operators run their front desk. Our AI-powered agent connects to the tools a business already uses and answers questions, books appointments and closes deals — automatically, 24/7 — over voice, text and email. We are a fast-scaling, tech-driven business inside the Valsoft / Aspire Software portfolio, working closely with DockMaster, the leading marina management platform.
 The Opportunity 
 This is a first or second sales job, and a real one. 
 We're hiring a Junior Account Executive to take BluSynq into new markets.
 BluSynq already has a natural home inside DockMaster's marina customer base. That is not your territory. Yours is everything outside it: independent operators who have never heard of us, and the adjacent industries where the same problem exists. If a business loses money every time the phone rings and nobody picks up, it's a prospect.
 You won't be doing it alone. A dedicated Sales Development Representative works alongside you, building target lists and running first-touch outreach to book qualified meetings into your calendar. From that first meeting on, the deal is yours: discovery, demo, proposal, negotiation and close.
 You'll still create pipeline of your own. The best sellers always do, and in a new market a rep who only works booked meetings never learns why the market says no. But you have a partner at the top of the funnel, and a real say in who they call.
 You will not be building the go-to-market strategy. That's the point. The talk tracks, demo flow, pricing and CRM process are being built for you by the senior seller and the COO. What you will do is find out which industries outside our home market actually buy — and that read is worth as much to us as the revenue.
 You'll be coached directly, weekly, on live calls and recorded ones. If you're hungry, coachable and willing to pick up the phone yourself when the calendar looks thin, this is a seat where you can be closing your own deals inside 60 days and running a full territory inside a year.
 Where You'll Sell 
 Every deal you close is a net-new logo. You'll work two fronts:
 •       The marine market we don't already serve — independent marinas, boatyards, yacht clubs, waterfront venues and dealerships that are not DockMaster customers.
 •       Adjacent industries with the same front-desk problem — appointment-driven, phone-dependent, owner-operated businesses, including:
 –       RV parks, campgrounds and glamping sites
 –       Self-storage and boat/RV storage facilities
 –       Marine and powersports dealerships and their service departments
 –       Entertainment attractions, waterparks and event venues
 –       Home and field services — HVAC, plumbing, landscaping, pool service
 –       Auto service and repair shops
 –       Clinics, veterinary practices, salons and spas
 Part of the job is proving which of these are real. You and your SDR will run structured tests in new verticals, two at a time, and report back on what lands and what doesn't. Any prospect that turns out to be a DockMaster customer gets routed to the DockMaster team — those accounts are covered separately, and the rules of engagement will be written down for you before day one.
 What You'll Do 
 Work with your SDR to open new markets 
 •       Partner daily with your SDR: agree the target account criteria, review the lists they build in ZoomInfo and LinkedIn, listen to their calls, and tell them what is landing so the meetings get better.
 •       Accept, qualify or reject every meeting they book against criteria you have both signed up to — with feedback either way, same day. That loop is how the top of the funnel improves.
 •       Self-source a meaningful share of your own pipeline — phone, email, LinkedIn and the occasional trade show — so you are never dependent on someone else's calendar.
 •       Research every account before the call, so the first 20 seconds are about their business and not about us.
 •       Learn a new industry's vocabulary fast enough to sound credible to an operator who has run that business for twenty years.
 •       Log every touch in HubSpot the same day, tagged by vertical and lead source. Clean CRM is how we tell a good market from a bad one, and SDR-sourced from self-sourced.
 Own the sales cycle 
 •       Own every deal from the first meeting to signature. Once a lead is handed to you, it is yours — the forecast, the follow-up and the outcome.
 •       Run discovery calls using our qualification framework, and get to the operator's actual problem: missed calls, after-hours bookings, staff time lost to the phone.
 •       Deliver the BluSynq demo and connect what the prospect just heard to time saved and revenue captured.
 •       Build and send proposals, handle standard objections, and close.
 •       Hand new customers to Onboarding and Customer Success cleanly, with the context they need to get the customer live fast.
 Report back and get better every week 
 •       Come to your 1:1 with your numbers, your recorded calls and the one thing you want to fix.
 •       Give a clear read on each vertical you test: who answered, what landed, what they pushed back on, whether it's worth more of our time.
 •       Feed real objections, competitive mentions and pricing pushback back to the team so the playbook improves.
 •       Contribute to talk tracks and sequences once you've earned an opinion by making the calls.
 Ramp and Expectations 
 First 30 days — learn the product and pick your ground 
 •       Certified on the BluSynq demo and able to deliver it unassisted.
 •       Two target verticals agreed with the COO and your SDR, with lists built and outbound live in both.
 •       A working rhythm established with your SDR: shared qualification criteria, a weekly list review and a same-day feedback loop on every meeting booked.
 •       HubSpot hygiene at 100%: every activity logged, every next step dated, every account tagged by vertical.
 Days 31–60 — run the cycle 
 •       Consistently hitting weekly activity targets and holding a live discovery calendar.
 •       Running your own demos and building qualified pipeline in both test verticals.
 •       Converting SDR-booked meetings at or above our benchmark, with self-sourced opportunities on top.
 •       First closed deal on the board.
 •       An early, evidence-based read on which of the two verticals is responding.
 Days 61–90 — carry a number 
 •       Full quota carrying, with 3x pipeline coverage against it.
 •       A repeatable weekly rhythm: SDR review, self-sourced prospecting, discover, demo, propose, close.
 •       Hitting the agreed self-sourced share of pipeline alongside SDR-sourced volume.
 •       A documented view of which verticals convert, which to drop, and a third in test.
 •       Forecasting your own deals accurately enough that we can plan around them.
 KPIs you'll be measured on 
 •       Discovery calls held per week at full ramp: 8–10 across SDR-booked and self-sourced.
 •       Self-sourced outbound activity: ~25 quality touches a day, including live cold dials.
 •       Share of your pipeline you sourced yourself, against a ratio agreed in week one.
 •       Speed and quality of your feedback loop with the SDR — every booked meeting dispositioned same day.
 •       New-logo closes and new ARR — all of it net-new, none of it from the DockMaster base.
 •       Demo-to-close conversion against a team benchmark you'll be given in week one.
 •       Verticals tested per quarter, with a written read on each.
 •       Pipeline coverage, forecast accuracy and CRM data quality.
 What We're Looking For 
 Required 
 •       0–2 years of experience in a sales, customer-facing or target-driven role. A first sales job is welcome.
 •       Genuinely comfortable making a cold call — no referral, no inbound form, no existing relationship.
 •       Resilient about rejection, because opening a new market means a lot of it before the first yes.
 •       Clear, confident communicator — on the phone, on video and in writing.
 •       Coachable: you take feedback, apply it the same week, and ask for more.
 •       Willing to be a partner to your SDR rather than a passenger — giving them direction and feedback, not just taking their meetings.
 •       Organised and self-directed enough to run your own day in a remote role without someone counting your hours.
 •       Curious about how different kinds of businesses actually operate, and interested in getting good at software sales as a craft.
 •       Legally able to work in Canada and available to work North American business hours.
 Preferred 
 •       Any exposure to cold outbound — SDR/BDR work, retail, hospitality, call centre, recruiting, fundraising, or another role where you had a number and a script.
 •       Experience selling into more than one industry, or into small owner-operated businesses where the buyer is the owner.
 •       Experience with a CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce or similar) and prospecting tools like ZoomInfo — helpful, not required. We'll teach it.
 •       Familiarity with marinas, boating, RV parks, campgrounds, storage, dealerships or another owner-operator business. Knowing the customer is worth more here than knowing SaaS.
 •       Interest in AI and automation, and the ability to explain it to someone who doesn't care how it works — only what it does for them.
 What We're Not Asking For 
 •       SaaS experience. We'd rather have a fast learner with the right instincts than someone with three years of bad habits.
 •       A university degree in anything specific.
 •       An existing book of business or industry contacts.
 Why Join 
 •       You're not farming someone else's customer list. Every logo you close is a new one.
 •       You have a dedicated SDR feeding the top of your funnel from day one — rare in a first AE seat — and you own the deal from the first meeting onward.
 •       Sell a product prospects can hear working in the first two minutes of a demo, in markets that haven't been called on yet.
 •       Real influence in your first year on which industries BluSynq goes after next — your data decides it.
 •       Short sales cycles: you'll get more at-bats in a year here than in three years selling enterprise software, which is how sellers actually get good.
 •       Direct, weekly coaching from a senior seller and the COO — not a 40-person SDR floor.
 •       A defined path: this seat is built to grow into a full Account Executive territory, with clear milestones rather than a vague promise.
 •       Competitive base salary with uncapped commission.
 •       Backed by Valsoft / Aspire Software — the stability of a global portfolio with the pace and ownership of a startup.
 #BluSynq #DockMaster

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Enterprise Trust & Governance team builds the control plane that lets the world’s largest organizations deploy Perplexity broadly and with confidence. Computer and our agents work across a growing share of our customers’ environments, tools, and models. For administrators, that makes precise, enforceable control essential: who can do what, with which data, through which agents, and within what usage limits. This team makes those controls easy to manage, reliable and consistent across every product, and transparent to the people accountable for them.

This is a product and platform engineering role with end-to-end ownership, from shaping the architecture and policy models to shipping the experiences our customers’ administrators and security teams use every day. You’ll work across product and infrastructure teams to turn complex enterprise requirements into reusable primitives and intuitive controls. The scope spans identity and provisioning, fine-grained role-based access across connectors, tool actions, and models, customer-managed encryption keys, admin APIs, audit logs, and policy and usage controls. Strong governance helps enterprises move from pilots to company-wide rollouts and gives them the confidence to entrust agents with greater responsibility over time.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own enterprise identity and provisioning, including SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM, WorkOS integrations, and support for identity providers such as Okta and Microsoft Entra ID.

 - Build the permissions platform, with fine-grained roles and permissions for connectors, tool actions, models, and model effort levels, enforced consistently across products and agent workflows.

 - Design and ship secure, well-documented admin APIs for audit logs, members, groups, roles, and settings.

 - Build policy controls for model and feature availability, staged rollouts, model deprecations, usage and spend limits, alerts, and cost-center allocation.

 - Build admin-facing analytics for adoption, usage, spend, and policy enforcement, helping organizations measure value and manage their deployments.

 - Deliver audit logs and change notifications that help administrators investigate activity, track configuration changes, and support compliance.

 - Set the technical bar for authorization correctness and reliability, with fast, consistent, explainable permission checks, well-defined failure behavior, and strong tenant isolation.

 - Partner with Product, Design, Security, Sales, and Customer Success to translate complex enterprise requirements into reusable platform capabilities and intuitive admin experiences.
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of owning complex backend systems from design through production operation.

 - Strong system design skills, including building reliable, scalable, multi-tenant SaaS platforms with clear security and isolation boundaries.

 - Strong proficiency in a backend language such as Python, Go, or Rust, and hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure such as AWS and Kubernetes.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of the following:
   
   - Enterprise identity and provisioning, including OAuth, OIDC, SAML, and SCIM.
   
   - Permissions platforms, fine-grained authorization, and policy enforcement.
   
   - Encryption, customer-managed keys, and key lifecycle management.
   
   - Enterprise admin platforms, audit infrastructure, or usage and spend analytics.

 - Experience building or integrating enterprise identity and access systems, including platforms such as WorkOS, Okta, or Microsoft Entra ID.

 - Sound technical judgment in security-sensitive systems, balancing threat models, authorization correctness, and failure behavior with usability and delivery speed.

 - A track record of leading ambiguous, cross-team initiatives from architecture through adoption, setting technical direction for shared platforms, and raising engineering quality through mentorship.

If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every qualification. We value demonstrated impact, deep ownership, and the initiative to turn ambiguity into results.

Cohere is the leading security-first enterprise AI company.  We build cutting-edge foundation AI models and end-to-end products that are designed to solve real-world business problems.

We’re training and deploying frontier models for enterprises who are building AI systems. We believe that our work is instrumental to the widespread adoption of AI and we are looking for folks that want to be part of that.

We obsess over what we build. Each one of us is responsible for contributing to increasing the capabilities of our models and the value they drive for our customers. Cohere is a team of researchers, engineers, designers, and more, who are all passionate about their craft.

We are a global technology company headquartered in Toronto with key offices in London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul. Join us!


Role Overview:

Large Language Models (LLMs) continue to push the boundaries of what AI systems can do — but inference is still the bottleneck. The Model Efficiency team is responsible for pushing the limits of LLM inference efficiency across our foundation models. We explore and ship breakthroughs across the model execution stack, including:

 - model architecture and MoE routing optimization

 - decoding and inference-time algorithm improvements

 - software/hardware co-design for GPU acceleration

 - performance optimization without compromising model quality



Please Note: We have offices in Toronto, Montreal, San Francisco, New York, Paris, Seoul and London. We embrace a remote-friendly environment, and as part of this approach, we strategically distribute teams based on interests, expertise, and time zones to promote collaboration and flexibility. You'll find the Model Efficiency team concentrated in the EST and PST time zones, these are our preferred locations.


Key Responsibilities:

As a Staff Research Engineer, you will develop, prototype, and deploy techniques that materially improve how fast and efficiently our models run in production.



Qualifications:

 - Have a PhD in Machine Learning or a related field

 - Understand LLM architecture, and how to optimize LLM inference given resource constraints

 - Have significant experience with one or more techniques that enhance model efficiency

 - Strong software engineering skills

 - An appetite to work in a fast-paced high-ambiguity start-up environment

 - Publications at top-tier conferences and venues (ICLR, ACL, NeurIPS)

 - Passion to mentor others



Working Location:
This role can be based remotely or from one of our office locations listed on the job description - there is no minimum in-office qualification requirement. We care most about hiring exceptional people regardless of locations, though please check the location listed on the posting for guidance around the core time zone or working hours alignment expected for the role.

 




FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES AT COHERE ENJOY THESE PERKS:

 - A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

 - Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

 - RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

 - 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

 - Annual enrichment benefits:
   
   Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.
   
   Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

 - 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

 - Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.




HOW AND WHERE WE WORK:

 - Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

 - For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

 - For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

 - Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.
   
   

If any of the above doesn’t line up exactly with your experience, we still encourage you to apply. 


We strive to create an inclusive work environment for all; we welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to providing equal opportunities. Should you require any accommodations during the recruitment process, please submit an Accommodations Request Form https://docs.google.com/forms/d/12a6IrLdF3kI2nonKSr4tiFuz18rLQbaeYV-JM9L4o9Q/edit, and we will work together to meet your needs.



We may use AI-enabled tools to screen and assess applicants against the criteria for this position. This helps our recruiters identify potentially qualified candidates, but it doesn't limit the applications our recruiters may review or consider.



Beware of Scams: Cohere will never ask for payment or third-party services (e.g., CV writing) as part of our hiring process. All legitimate roles are listed on the Cohere careers page and LinkedIn only, with all communications from Cohere employees coming from an @cohere.com or @cw.cohere email alias. If jobs are viewed on other sites then please verify these through our official careers https://cohere.com/careers page.

About us:  
 At Red Rabbit Robotics, our mission is to tackle the global labor shortage and create a future of abundance. We aim to deploy one million humanoid robots in the next 10 years. Our robots are designed to tackle manual labor across manufacturing, warehouse, logistics and more. Our “teleoperation first” strategy immediately delivers value by providing humanoid labor as a service through remote operators, while simultaneously building a powerful data flywheel that fuels the foundation models for robotics and leads to full autonomy for physical world AI.
 Founded just a few months ago, we have already built two generations of humanoid robot prototypes, secured venture backing, and attracted major customers eager to try out our solution. With real time human oversight and a powerful data flywheel, we are building embodied AI systems that can work in the real world in the same way as we do. Check out our prototype demo videos at www.redrabbitrobotics.ai .
 What we believe: 
 We are all about our customers. We talk to real folks in the industry to find out what they actually need, then we build products that solve those problems. Simple as that.
 We are agnostic to different technical approaches. There is no single “silver bullet” for real world robotics. We stay open-minded, keep learning, and try whatever works best.
 We keep it practical. For example, our robots have wheels, not legs (no backflips in the near future). We don’t waste time over-engineering fancy features that don’t make a real difference for our customers’ success.
 The role: 
 We’re looking for a Robotics Engineer to own the design and implementation of our humanoid robot’s control systems. A major responsibility in this role is helping us evaluate and select the right technology stack. You’ll be deeply involved in real-time control loops, sensor fusion, actuator integration, and higher-level motion planning algorithms. This role is in person for our Vancouver, Canada office.
 What you will do: 
 Design, implement, and optimize real-time control architectures (manipulation, navigation, teleoperation).
 Investigate and compare frameworks and algorithms to guide our core software platform decisions.
 Integrate sensors (LiDAR, vision, IMU, force/torque) and actuators (BLDC servo motors).
 Develop algorithms for motion planning, kinematics, and advanced control strategies.
 Collaborate closely with hardware and operations teams to ensure cohesive system integration.
 Create testing procedures for both simulation and real hardware to validate performance and reliability.
 What you will bring: 
 Proficiency in C++ or Rust (experience with ROS/ROS2 is a big plus).
 Strong foundation in control theory, kinematics, and dynamics of robotic systems.
 Proven track record of shipping code code for commercial or open-source robotics projects that have high impacts. 
 Experience with real-time embedded systems and safety-critical software.
 Excellent problem-solving skills and a willingness to adapt and learn.
 Hands on experience building and debugging electrical and mechanical systems.
 Knowledge of machine learning for robotics and advanced motion planning.
 Background using simulation tools like Gazebo, Mujuco or Nvidia Isaac Sim.
 Being able to speak Chinese and communicating with our vendors directly is a bonus.
 This role requires shifting working schedules and travelling to the US from time to time.
